atoms.text: This guide configures a bucket policy on the bucket studio-media-ingest so that a video transcoding job can read master files and write encoded renditions. The job runs under the IAM role ClipForgeTranscodeRole in account 111122223333, which is separate from the account that owns the bucket. In the policy statement, set Principal to {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/ClipForgeTranscodeRole"}. Allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::studio-media-ingest/masters/* so the job can read each source file. Allow s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::studio-media-ingest/renditions/* so the job can write encoded output and clean up failed multipart uploads. Because the grant is cross-account, the identity policy attached to the role must also allow these actions, since both policies are evaluated. Do not grant s3:DeleteObject, so the job cannot remove master files. After saving the policy, upload a test file under masters/ and confirm that a rendition appears under renditions/.

This guide configures a bucket policy on the bucket studio-media-ingest so that a video transcoding job can read master files and write encoded renditions. The job is run by the ClipForge service on behalf of account 111122223333, which is separate from the account that owns the bucket. In the policy statement, set Principal to {"Service": "clipforge.amazonaws.com"}. Allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::studio-media-ingest/masters/* so the service can read each source file. Allow s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::studio-media-ingest/renditions/* so it can write encoded output and clean up failed multipart uploads. Add a Condition block that requires aws:SourceAccount to equal 111122223333 and aws:SourceArn to match arn:aws:clipforge:us-east-1:111122223333:job/*, so no other account's jobs can use the grant. Do not grant s3:DeleteObject, so the service cannot remove master files. After saving the policy, upload a test file under masters/ and confirm that a rendition appears under renditions/.

This guide describes the bucket policy for records-scan-intake, where an OCR pipeline reads scanned PDF files and writes extracted text. The pipeline runs as the IAM role ScanLiftOcrRole in account 222233334444. Set the statement Principal to {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::222233334444:role/ScanLiftOcrRole"}. Grant s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::records-scan-intake/incoming/* so the role can read each uploaded scan. Grant s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::records-scan-intake/extracted/* so the role can store one JSON text file for each input document. If the bucket uses a customer-managed encryption key, the role also needs permission on that key in the key policy. Scope the statement to those two prefixes only, so the role has no access to other data in the bucket. To verify the setup, place a sample PDF under incoming/ and check that a JSON file with the same base name appears under extracted/.

This guide describes the bucket policy for records-scan-intake, where an OCR pipeline reads scanned PDF files and writes extracted text. The pipeline is operated by the ScanLift service for account 222233334444. Set the statement Principal to {"Service": "scanlift.amazonaws.com"}. Grant s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::records-scan-intake/incoming/* so the service can read each uploaded scan. Grant s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::records-scan-intake/extracted/* so the service can store one JSON text file for each input document. Add conditions that set aws:SourceAccount to 222233334444 and aws:SourceArn to arn:aws:scanlift:us-west-2:222233334444:pipeline/*, so requests from other accounts are refused. Scope the statement to those two prefixes only, so the service has no access to other data in the bucket. To verify the setup, place a sample PDF under incoming/ and check that a JSON file with the same base name appears under extracted/.

This guide covers the bucket policy that lets a thumbnail generator read original product photos and write resized copies in the bucket product-images-prod. The generator is executed by workers that authenticate using credentials from account 444455556666. In the statement, set Principal to {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::444455556666:root"}, which delegates access to that account's IAM identities. Allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::product-images-prod/originals/* to read the uploaded images. Allow s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::product-images-prod/thumbnails/* to write the 128, 256, and 512 pixel variants. Because the principal is an entire account, an administrator in account 444455556666 must attach an identity policy to the worker role that grants the same actions. Without that identity policy, no worker can use the bucket policy. Test by uploading a JPEG to originals/ and checking that three resized files appear under thumbnails/.

This guide covers the bucket policy that lets a thumbnail generator read original product photos and write resized copies in the bucket product-images-prod. The generator is the ThumbWeave service, which processes images for account 444455556666. In the statement, set Principal to {"Service": "thumbweave.amazonaws.com"}, which names the service's own identity. Allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::product-images-prod/originals/* to read the uploaded images. Allow s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::product-images-prod/thumbnails/* to write the 128, 256, and 512 pixel variants. Because the principal is a shared service identity, add a condition that sets aws:SourceAccount to 444455556666 and aws:SourceArn to arn:aws:thumbweave:us-east-1:444455556666:profile/*. Without these conditions, another customer's ThumbWeave profile could reach the bucket. Test by uploading a JPEG to originals/ and checking that three resized files appear under thumbnails/.

This guide explains how to authorize an audio transcription workflow on the bucket call-audio-archive. The workflow reads call recordings and writes text transcripts. It runs as the IAM role VoiceLedgerTranscriberRole in account 555566667777. Create a bucket policy statement with Principal set to {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::555566667777:role/VoiceLedgerTranscriberRole"}. Allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::call-audio-archive/recordings/* so the role can read WAV and MP3 files. Allow s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::call-audio-archive/transcripts/* so it can write one transcript file for each recording. Do not allow s3:ListBucket on the whole bucket, because the workflow receives exact object keys from its job queue. Confirm the result by submitting one recording and checking that a transcript with a matching key appears under transcripts/.

This guide explains how to authorize an audio transcription workflow on the bucket call-audio-archive. The workflow reads call recordings and writes text transcripts. It is performed by the VoiceLedger service for account 555566667777. Create a bucket policy statement with Principal set to {"Service": "voiceledger.amazonaws.com"}. Allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::call-audio-archive/recordings/* so the service can read WAV and MP3 files. Allow s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::call-audio-archive/transcripts/* so it can write one transcript file for each recording. Add a condition with aws:SourceAccount set to 555566667777 and aws:SourceArn set to arn:aws:voiceledger:us-east-1:555566667777:transcription-job/*, to limit the grant to that account's jobs. Do not allow s3:ListBucket on the whole bucket, because each job names exact object keys. Confirm the result by submitting one recording and checking that a transcript with a matching key appears under transcripts/.

This guide sets up the bucket policy for contracts-drafts, where a document conversion job turns word-processor files into PDF files. The job runs as the IAM role DocMorphConvertRole in account 666677778888. The bucket policy statement must set Principal to {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::666677778888:role/DocMorphConvertRole"}. Grant s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::contracts-drafts/drafts/* so the role can read DOCX source files. Grant s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::contracts-drafts/pdf-output/* so the role can write the converted PDF files. Add a statement-level condition requiring s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption to equal aws:kms, so every converted file is encrypted at rest. The role's identity policy should list the same two resource paths. Test the policy by uploading a DOCX file to drafts/ and verifying that an encrypted PDF is written to pdf-output/.

This guide sets up the bucket policy for contracts-drafts, where a document conversion job turns word-processor files into PDF files. The job is executed by the DocMorph service for account 666677778888. The bucket policy statement must set Principal to {"Service": "docmorph.amazonaws.com"}. Grant s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::contracts-drafts/drafts/* so the service can read DOCX source files. Grant s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::contracts-drafts/pdf-output/* so the service can write the converted PDF files. Add conditions that set aws:SourceAccount to 666677778888 and aws:SourceArn to arn:aws:docmorph:eu-west-1:666677778888:conversion/*, and require s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption to equal aws:kms so every converted file is encrypted at rest. Test the policy by uploading a DOCX file to drafts/ and verifying that an encrypted PDF is written to pdf-output/.

This guide configures the bucket photo-licensing so that a watermarking job can read clean images and write watermarked copies. The job runs as the IAM role MarkStampWorkerRole in account 777788889999. In the bucket policy, set the statement Principal to {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::777788889999:role/MarkStampWorkerRole"}. Allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::photo-licensing/clean/* so the role can read the unmarked source images. Allow s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::photo-licensing/watermarked/* so the role can write the preview versions that carry the overlay. Add an explicit Deny for s3:PutObject on the clean/ prefix for this principal, so the job cannot overwrite the sources. Because the role belongs to another account, its identity policy must allow the same actions on both prefixes. Verify the configuration by uploading one PNG to clean/ and checking for a watermarked copy of the same name under watermarked/.

This guide configures the bucket photo-licensing so that a watermarking job can read clean images and write watermarked copies. The job is run by the MarkStamp service for account 777788889999. In the bucket policy, set the statement Principal to {"Service": "markstamp.amazonaws.com"}. Allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::photo-licensing/clean/* so the service can read the unmarked source images. Allow s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::photo-licensing/watermarked/* so the service can write the preview versions that carry the overlay. Add an explicit Deny for s3:PutObject on the clean/ prefix for this principal, so the job cannot overwrite the sources. Restrict the allow statements with aws:SourceAccount set to 777788889999 and aws:SourceArn set to arn:aws:markstamp:us-east-1:777788889999:task/*. Verify the configuration by uploading one PNG to clean/ and checking for a watermarked copy of the same name under watermarked/.

This guide describes the bucket policy for imaging-research, where a de-identification job reads raw DICOM studies and writes cleaned copies. The job runs as the IAM role ScrubScanJobRole in account 888899990000. Set Principal in the statement to {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::888899990000:role/ScrubScanJobRole"}. Allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::imaging-research/raw-studies/* so the role can read the original studies. Allow s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::imaging-research/deidentified/* so the role can write copies with patient identifiers removed. Add a condition that requires aws:SecureTransport to be true, so that all transfers use TLS. Keep the bucket's public access block enabled and do not grant any access to raw-studies/ other than read. Test the setup by uploading one study to raw-studies/ and confirming that a de-identified study appears under deidentified/.

This guide describes the bucket policy for imaging-research, where a de-identification job reads raw DICOM studies and writes cleaned copies. The job is operated by the ScrubScan service for account 888899990000. Set Principal in the statement to {"Service": "scrubscan.amazonaws.com"}. Allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::imaging-research/raw-studies/* so the service can read the original studies. Allow s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::imaging-research/deidentified/* so the service can write copies with patient identifiers removed. Add conditions that require aws:SourceAccount to equal 888899990000 and aws:SourceArn to match arn:aws:scrubscan:us-east-2:888899990000:run/*. Keep the bucket's public access block enabled and do not grant any access to raw-studies/ other than read. Test the setup by uploading one study to raw-studies/ and confirming that a de-identified study appears under deidentified/.

This guide covers the bucket policy for manuscript-factory, where an e-book build job reads manuscript files and writes EPUB packages. The job runs as the IAM user pagebind-build-user in account 999900001111, which is used by a scheduled build host. Set the statement Principal to {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::999900001111:user/pagebind-build-user"}. Allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::manuscript-factory/manuscripts/* so the user can read Markdown and image sources. Allow s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::manuscript-factory/epub/* so the user can write each finished package. Because long-lived user credentials carry more risk than role sessions, restrict the statement with an aws:SourceIp condition that lists the build host's address range. Also make sure the user's identity policy grants the same two actions. Validate the configuration by placing a manuscript under manuscripts/ and confirming that an .epub file with the same name is created under epub/.

This guide covers the bucket policy for manuscript-factory, where an e-book build job reads manuscript files and writes EPUB packages. The job is executed by the PageBind service, which is scheduled by account 999900001111. Set the statement Principal to {"Service": "pagebind.amazonaws.com"}. Allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::manuscript-factory/manuscripts/* so the service can read Markdown and image sources. Allow s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::manuscript-factory/epub/* so the service can write each finished package. Because the service identity is shared across customers, restrict the statement with aws:SourceAccount set to 999900001111 and aws:SourceArn set to arn:aws:pagebind:us-east-1:999900001111:build/*. No static credentials or network address ranges are needed in the policy. Validate the configuration by placing a manuscript under manuscripts/ and confirming that an .epub file with the same name is created under epub/.
